shorts.title: Did 300 Years of History Never Happen? 🕳️ Verdict on the Viral One #1
shorts.description:
A German author added up the Middle Ages, and found three centuries missing. The Phantom Time theory (Heribert Illig, 1991) says AD 614 to 911 were invented, so it's really about 1729. Busted: Chinese astronomers logged Halley's Comet in 837 right where orbital math puts it, eclipse records and tree-ring chronologies line up, and the 1582 calendar fix only reset the calendar to AD 325, not to Julius Caesar's time.

shorts.title: The Man With Two Faces Never Existed 😳 Verdict on the Viral One #2
shorts.description:
A newspaper printed a man with two faces, and people believed it. Edward Mordrake (Mordake), the English heir with a whispering second face, first appeared on 8 December 1895 in the Boston Sunday Post, in an article by fiction writer Charles Lotin Hildreth that cited a 'Royal Scientific Society' that didn't exist then. A medical encyclopedia copied it in 1896 from that 'lay source'. No record of the man has ever been found.
